comparison: Both strongly support the structural determination of SLC26A6 (C4, C57-C66). OpenEval emphasizes the 3.3 Å cryo-EM resolution and structural comparisons with SLC26A9. Peer reviewers unanimously praise the 'novel cryo-EM structure' and 'first partial view of the STAS domain.' However, OpenEval R1 covers additional claims (C70-C83) about detailed structural comparisons that peer R1 does not explicitly address.

Both address structural comparisons with SLC26A9 (C72-C79). OpenEval R1 includes these claims as part of broader structural characterization with RMSD values. Peer R4 accepts these structural comparisons, with Reviewer 2 noting 'close resemblance to...SLC26A9' and Reviewer 3 stating 'structural details...are well-conserved among SLC26s.'

Perfect agreement on electroneutral exchange characterization (C40-C50). Both evaluations strongly support the claims with converging evidence from multiple assays. OpenEval cites patch clamp, lucigenin-based Cl- flux, and europium probe data. Peer reviewers use terms like 'unequivocally' and 'compelling evidence' for the electroneutral Cl-/HCO3- exchange. Peer R2 additionally includes C5, C56, C112 as part of this evaluation.

Both address oxalate transport (C52-C55, C113, C116-C117) but with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the ACMA assay data robust and the inference of electrogenic transport 'logically sound.' Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 identifying 'inconsistent, technique-dependent detection' as a weakness, particularly the failure to detect whole cell currents while observing ACMA fluorescence decay.

Strong agreement on structural basis for selectivity differences (C7, C90-C102, C120-C124). Both evaluations support the identification of Arg404 as a key residue and the structural analysis of pocket geometry. OpenEval emphasizes RMSD calculations and structural data. Peer reviewers note the authors 'define a residue...which explains part of the difference' and discuss how 'size and charge variance of the binding pocket' contributes to mechanistic differences.

Perfect claim overlap (C103-C111) with agreement on R404V mutation effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes it as 'well-designed structure-function experiment' showing uncoupled transport and loss of coupled exchange. Peer Reviewer 1 confirms the mutation 'yields apparently uncoupled electrogenic chloride transport' but notes as a weakness the 'incomplete explanation' since single mutation is insufficient for full conversion to SLC26A9-like function.

Both address mechanistic differences between paralogs (C129-C135) but with different confidence. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, stating the mechanistic model 'provides a coherent explanation' while acknowledging 'exact energy barriers remain to be fully elucidated.' Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 identifying 'incomplete explanation of mechanistic determinants' as a weakness and authors acknowledging the basis 'is currently still unclear.'

Perfect claim overlap (C86-C89, C125-C128) on structural conservation within SLC26 family. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes RMSD comparison with Prestin and conserved arginine residue. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly supports this, calling it 'an interesting discussion comparing the structures of SLC26A5, SLC26A6, and SLC26A9' and how binding site details 'might influence the mechanistic distinctions.'

Strong agreement on uncertainty regarding IVS region functional role (C62, C67, C137-C143). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes 'functional implications are largely speculative' and 'mechanistic understanding is incomplete.' Peer reviewers do not explicitly validate or challenge these interpretations, and the authors use speculative language like 'presumably influences' and 'might have contributed.'

Both address limitations in mechanistic understanding (C132-C135) but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, praising the 'honest assessment of uncertainties' and noting appropriate acknowledgment of knowledge gaps. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 identifying this as a weakness regarding 'incomplete explanation of mechanistic determinants' of coupling vs. uncoupled transport.

Perfect claim overlap (C26-C27, C35-C38) on SLC26A9 functional properties. Both rate as SUPPORTED. These are established findings from prior work serving as controls and context. OpenEval notes they are 'well-supported by citations' and provide 'functional context.' Peer reviewers accept these as benchmarks, with Reviewer 3 noting the 'functional comparison with SLC26A9' as a strength.

High claim overlap (27 shared claims) on background/context. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval states the background 'establishes the scientific rationale' and is 'well-documented with appropriate citations.' Peer reviewers do not challenge these established facts, with the editor noting the study 'provides broadly relevant insights' in the context of known SLC26 diversity.

Minimal overlap (C6 only) but related content. OpenEval R12 addresses prior structural work on SLC26A9 (C3, C6, C68-C69, C84-C85) as framework for interpreting SLC26A6. Peer R4 addresses structural comparisons between the two paralogs (C6, C72-C79). Both support the structural similarity and use prior SLC26A9 work as context.

Both address summary/concluding observations. OpenEval R13 focuses solely on summary claim C144, rating it SUPPORTED as accurately reflecting study contributions. Peer R12 addresses supporting observations and summary statements (C119, C136, C140, C142, C144), implicitly accepting them with the editor's assessment that this is an 'important manuscript' providing 'broadly relevant insights.'

Minimal overlap (C112 only). OpenEval R6 synthesizes mechanistic differences including electroneutral exchange by SLC26A6. Peer R2 comprehensively evaluates the electroneutral exchange characterization (C40-C50, C112) with strong support from all reviewers. Both agree on the electroneutral exchange mechanism.

Minimal overlap (C136 only). OpenEval R9 addresses limitations and acknowledges 'lack of pronounced differences in core-gate contacts between paralogs' (C136). Peer R12 implicitly accepts this observation as part of supporting details without explicit comment.

Minimal overlap (C140, C142). OpenEval R8 discusses IVS region and C-terminal extensions with uncertainty about functional roles. Peer R12 implicitly accepts these observations as supporting details without challenging the speculative interpretations about C-terminal extensions.

Minimal overlap (C3 only). OpenEval R12 focuses on prior SLC26A9 structural work as framework. Peer R11 addresses broader background context including C3 among many other claims. Both accept prior structural work as established context.

Minimal overlap (C5, C56). OpenEval R1 includes these as part of structural characterization. Peer R2 includes them as part of electroneutral exchange functional characterization. Different focus but no disagreement.

Minimal overlap (C80-C83). OpenEval R1 includes these claims about substrate binding site and chloride ion as part of comprehensive structural characterization. Peer R5 addresses broader selectivity differences including these structural details. Both support the structural observations.

Minimal overlap (C119 only) regarding similar Cl- affinities between paralogs. OpenEval R6 includes this as part of mechanistic synthesis. Peer R12 implicitly accepts this observation without explicit comment.
